meta.title: Aethyr for Unreal Engine 5: AI that speaks Blueprint
meta.description: An MCP server that lets any MCP client read and author Unreal Engine 5 Blueprints in plain language. 301 tools. No editor scripting.

title: AI THAT SPEAKS
BLUEPRINT
hero.sub: Point your AI assistant at your project and just ask. It reads and rewrites your Unreal Engine 5 Blueprints in plain language.

install.lead: Or let your assistant install it:
install.prompt: Get Aethyr from aethyr.gg and set it up for my Unreal project.

badges.label: Auto-backup before each asset's first save

features.heading:
An arsenal your AI
can actually wield.

cards.title: See everything
cards.body: Variables, functions, graphs, nodes, components, interfaces, timelines: your AI reads the whole structure of a Blueprint, no guessing.

cards.title: Author by asking
cards.body: “Add a dash ability with a 2-second cooldown.” It spawns the variables, wires the nodes, and compiles—the way you'd do it by hand, but spoken.

cards.title: Safety rails built in
cards.body: Batched Blueprint writes compile before they save, and a failed compile rolls the batch back. Each asset is backed up before its first save. Powerful tools like Python, config edits and deletes are there too, and they're explicit. One env var turns on read-only.

cards.title: All-or-nothing batches
cards.body: Chain a dozen edits into one transaction. If step seven fails, the whole thing rolls back; your graph is never left half-rewritten.

cards.title: Your AI, your client
cards.body: Speaks the Model Context Protocol, so it works with any MCP client, Claude included. Open your client in your Unreal project folder and go.

cards.title: Runs in the dark
cards.body: Drives a headless editor or talks to a live one over a socket, auto-routing per call. No babysitting an editor window required.

clients.heading: Works with any stdio MCP client.

snippet.heading: Paste and go.
snippet.caption: Or add it by hand. AETHYR_PROJECT is optional, and only needed if your client doesn't start in the project folder. Run AethyrMcp.exe config --client=<name> to print this filled in for your client.

compare.heading:
Built to work with
Epic's own MCP
compare.note: UE 5.8 ships Epic's experimental MCP server, and Aethyr connects to it. You get Epic's toolsets plus everything Aethyr adds on top.

rows.feature: Batches that roll back if the compile fails
Backup before an asset's first save
Set up by asking your AI

steps.title: Bind your AI
steps.body: Ask your assistant to set it up, or run setup. It adds Aethyr to your MCP client for you, and edits no project files.

steps.title: Speak the intent
steps.body: Ask in plain language. “What does BP_Enemy do?” “Refactor this into a function.” “Give the player a double-jump.”

steps.title: Watch it weave
steps.body: It reads, edits, compiles, and saves on the real asset. Batches are all-or-nothing, and each asset is backed up before its first save. You review the diff.

items.a: Batched Blueprint writes (apply_ops) go through a compile gate, and a failed compile rolls the whole batch back with nothing written. Single-step writes save as they go, unless you set AETHYR_STRICT_COMPILE=1. A backup copy of the on-disk asset is made before the first save of each asset in a session. Tools like Python scripting and config edits skip those checks, so use read-only mode if you only want to look.

items.q: Does it send data to the cloud?
items.a: No telemetry and no analytics. Your project never leaves your machine. The GitHub build checks GitHub for new releases about once a day (turn that off with AETHYR_UPDATE_CHECK=0). The Fab build makes no network calls of its own.
Writes are on by default in every build. Set AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1 for any session where you only want to look.

items.q: Does it need the Unreal Editor open?
items.a: No. Aethyr auto-routes each call: if an editor is running on the project it connects to the live session; otherwise it drives a headless editor automatically. No babysitting an editor window required.

items.q: Which MCP clients does it support?
items.a: Any client that speaks the stdio MCP transport—Claude (Anthropic), Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, and others. If your client can load an MCP server, Aethyr works with it.
Aethyr 0.5.0 and later need UE 5.8 or later, which is compile-checked and live-tested on every release.

summon.heading:
Every tool.
Full access.
summon.body: One build with the whole tool surface and writes on by default. Set one env var if you want a read-only session.
